museo-fortuny.title: Venice — Museo Fortuny
museo-fortuny.excerpt: A visit to Mariano Fortuny’s former home in Venice: studios, textiles, murals, and a surprising cardboard cloister.
museo-fortuny.body:
In Venice I visited Museo Fortuny, drawn first by the architecture and how the spaces were planned. The museum was once the home of artist Mariano Fortuny, with his painting studio, textile workshop, and collections of paintings, fabrics, and sculpture.

On the ground floor, the Winter Garden is lined with murals that called to mind the artist’s final masterpiece in Maugham’s *The Moon and Sixpence* — a quiet, heartfelt moment.

At the end of the route came an unexpected surprise: a cloister of delicate craftsmanship and careful lighting. When I realised it was built from corrugated cardboard, I walked through again and again, looking for every detail I had missed.

Highly recommended if you are travelling to Venice — a museum with a character all its own.

the-box-museum.title: The Box Museum
the-box-museum.excerpt: Plymouth’s The Box, Manor Street Galleries, and a Stanhope Forbes painting worth seeking out.
the-box-museum.body:
On this trip to Plymouth we visited The Box museum, a newer gallery, and Manor Street Galleries, a pub that shows local artists’ work.

Unexpectedly, The Box holds some Turner sketches — but the painting we loved most was by Stanhope Alexander Forbes (see above). A photo can only hint at it; if you go, look for this oil.

Manor Street Galleries also has engaging pieces at more approachable prices than many commercial galleries — worth a visit if you want to support artists or bring art home.

uk-anytime-day-train-ticket.title: The upside of UK Anytime Day train tickets
uk-anytime-day-train-ticket.excerpt: How an Anytime Day ticket can let you hop on and off between towns on the same day.
uk-anytime-day-train-ticket.body:
UK train tickets come in many forms. With an Anytime Day ticket you can leave and re-enter stations between your start and end points as often as you like that day. For example, travelling from city A to city D, you can get off in towns B and C along the way — so with a well-planned itinerary, one ticket can cover several places.

It is not always the cheapest option; time-restricted fares can be better value. Still, it is useful information when you plan.

The photos show a train in Wales (with power and USB sockets) and ticket details explaining the flexibility of a day single.

villa-necchi-campiglio.title: Villa Necchi Campiglio
villa-necchi-campiglio.excerpt: Milan’s house museums and the Case Museo Card — design that stopped me in my tracks.
villa-necchi-campiglio.body:
While planning Milan beyond the Duomo, I found several former private homes now open as museums. I bought a Case Museo Card and visited four house museums — eye-opening in every sense.

The photo shows a design detail at Villa Necchi Campiglio that I found especially striking.

A single adult ticket is usually about €15; the Case Museo Card is about €25 (roughly NT$880) and covers one visit to each of four museums within a year of purchase.

Details and the card: https://casemuseo.it/en/la-card-eng/

scuola-grande-di-san-rocco.title: Scuola Grande di San Rocco
scuola-grande-di-san-rocco.excerpt: A quiet Venetian treasure: Tintoretto’s hall that left me speechless — and only €10 to enter.
scuola-grande-di-san-rocco.body:
Sometimes while travelling you pass a place that simply feels different, and you stop to take a few photos. That is how I found Scuola Grande di San Rocco, wandering Venice’s lanes — drawn in by a refined stillness, then astonished once inside.

The ground-floor paintings are already worth the visit. Climb the stone stairs into the upper hall and your jaw drops: every surface is carved and painted, almost too much to take in.

When my neck ached from looking up, I found the large mirrors the museum provides on the long table to the left at the top of the stairs — heavy to hold, so the strain just moves to your arms. There is a third floor too, with religious objects and a mural under restoration.

Afterwards I found surprisingly little about it on blogs or even the official site. I hope more visitors to Venice discover it — excellent value at only €10 (about NT$340).

singapore-solo-trip.title: A solo day in Singapore
singapore-solo-trip.excerpt: Nine hours, 30,000 steps: Supertree Grove, Cloud Forest, Chinatown, Arab Street, and Changi.
singapore-solo-trip.body:
I walked Singapore’s city centre for nine hours and more than 30,000 steps — the Supertree skyway, Cloud Forest (a favourite), across two bridges, along the waterfront to Chinatown, then by MRT to the Arab Quarter, and back to Changi Airport.

In 25–30°C weather I soaked up vitamin D and plenty of sweat. At Changi I booked a shower at the Changi Lounge (Terminal 1, level 1), collected left luggage, freshened up, and wrote this from the lounge with my phone charging.

My first solo trip to Singapore — grateful that everything went smoothly, and that I packed a full day of wonder into one layover.

multi-city-flights.title: How to add an extra stop when booking flights
multi-city-flights.excerpt: Using Skyscanner multi-city search to visit Singapore on the way between Taipei and London.
multi-city-flights.body:
Back in Taiwan I saw the people I needed to see, ate what I had been craving, and did what I had hoped to do — grateful for it all.

For the return, I used Skyscanner’s multi-city tool in two legs: 1) Taipei to Singapore, 2) Singapore to London. It was cheaper than a direct Taiwan–UK search, and gave me an extra day in Singapore.

With the same approach on this trip I also added Milan, Venice, and Singapore. Recommended for travellers who want more places for less.

venice.title: Venice
venice.excerpt: A city of walkways and waterways — gondolas, water taxis, and remarkably skilled boat drivers.
venice.body:
Working while travelling, a week disappeared quickly — including a trip to Venice that taught me so much.

Every street is for pedestrians; there are no cars. Besides the walkways there are canals: family boats, tourist gondolas, water taxis, ambulances, police boats, rubbish boats. Everyone steers with impressive skill.

Gondolas are longer than they look. One day an ambulance appeared and gondoliers edged aside in the narrow channel with calm precision so it could pass — I almost applauded.

cardiff-christmas-market.title: Cardiff Christmas market
cardiff-christmas-market.excerpt: Salt on the ground like frost, mulled wine in the air, and Christmas songs before December.
cardiff-christmas-market.body: At the weekend we went to the Christmas market in Cardiff, capital of Wales. It was cold; salt on the ground to stop ice looked almost like frost and added to the winter mood. Mulled wine filled the air, carols filled the ears — not yet December, but the festive feeling was already strong.

poetry-autumn.title: Poetry in autumn
poetry-autumn.excerpt: Why autumn is a season for poetry — and how rhythm lives beyond the page.
poetry-autumn.body:
Autumn is a season made for reading poetry.

The other day a student said poetry always felt a hundred thousand miles away. I know he loves music, so I asked whether he likes rap. He understood at once and smiled.

Much of poetry’s beauty is rhythm — but rhythm is not only formal metre. It is everywhere. Artists try, through every medium, to gather from nature or from the cosmos they sense a rhythm of beauty.

In this windy season that rhythm feels especially close. Quiet down and listen, and you may find it.

two-poems.title: Two poems
two-poems.excerpt: A weekend of art with musician friends in Devon, and two short poems from before and after meeting Mr Ma.
two-poems.body:
A few days ago we had an unforgettable weekend.

We visited musician friends in Devon who share our love of art — walking in the woods, painting, playing music, reading poems, and sharing good food.

Making art alone is a joy; making it together, trading ideas, is another kind of thrill.

Here are two short poems I wrote years ago — the first in 2011 before I met Mr Ma, the second after.

**(I)**  
It happened before, it can happen again  
You said I'm your one, I'm your only friend  
But when the night falls and the silence grows  
I wonder where that promise goes

**(II)**  
In the quiet of this room I find  
A hand that steadies heart and mind  
Not every storm must leave us cold  
Some winters teach us how to hold

aurora-in-wales.title: Aurora in Wales
aurora-in-wales.excerpt: Woken at night in South Wales to see the northern lights near Brecon Beacons.
aurora-in-wales.body:
I had been asleep when Mr Ma, still working, woke me to see the aurora — a tip from his boss who was also still at work. Grateful for the chance; I finally saw the northern lights.

We were in South Wales, about a 25-minute drive from Brecon Beacons National Park.

cardiff-capital.title: Cardiff — the capital
cardiff-capital.excerpt: A quick walk through Royal Arcade, Cardiff’s oldest shopping arcade since 1858.
cardiff-capital.body: In Cardiff, the “City of Arcades,” even a hurried visit should include a stroll through an arcade. Royal Arcade is Cardiff’s oldest, open since 1858.

prince-of-wales-cardiff.title: Cardiff — The Prince of Wales pub
prince-of-wales-cardiff.excerpt: A theatre turned Wetherspoon pub, careful interiors, and excellent spicy chicken wings.
prince-of-wales-cardiff.body:
In Cardiff on business I found The Prince of Wales — a former theatre now run by Wetherspoon.

I like many of their pubs across the UK: they offer a sense of safety for those who need it, and they care about restoring and keeping each building’s character.

Also: their spicy chicken wings are excellent.

cafe-tirolerhof-vienna.title: Vienna café — Café Tirolerhof
cafe-tirolerhof-vienna.excerpt: Old-world elegance, newspapers on rods, and apple strudel in the middle of tourist Vienna.
cafe-tirolerhof-vienna.body:
In a short stay in Vienna, Café Tirolerhof stayed with me — right among tourists and luxury shops, yet keeping a last-century elegance.

Newspapers are clipped neatly for reading. Staff bring your drink with a welcome glass of water — perhaps to balance a sweet hot chocolate, or to cleanse the palate. In a city where water can cost more than wine, it felt like a small gift.

The apple strudel was soft, gently sweet with a touch of tartness.

swansea.title: Swansea — Wales’s second city
swansea.excerpt: Gin & Juice: a tucked-away rooftop restaurant with sea views and a satisfying meal.
swansea.body:
A few days ago we walked around Swansea with friends and found Gin & Juice — a distinctive restaurant. The ground-floor entrance is in a passageway with only a simple board; we did not expect much, just a reasonable place to eat.

Upstairs (lift or stairs) the room opens out, and the sea view at the far end is striking — though the seaside seats were closed for ceiling work.

I had grilled fish; the two men had different burgers. We were all glad we came.

red-kite-feeding-station.title: Red kite feeding station
red-kite-feeding-station.excerpt: Near Rhayader, watching birds once nearly extinct — now more than two hundred strong.
red-kite-feeding-station.body:
Near the mid-Wales town of Rhayader is a Red Kite Feeding Station; we bought tickets for this trip.

Around 1900 red kites nearly vanished — only three pairs left — after hunting and egg collecting. After more than a century of conservation there are over two hundred birds, all descended from one pair. We learned this at the National Showcaves Centre for Wales the day before; it is extraordinary.

Wales has several feeding farms where bird lovers can watch red kites up close — a moving conservation story.

elan-valley.title: Elan Valley
elan-valley.excerpt: Wales’s “Lake District”: reservoirs, countryside, and the Elan Valley Trail.
elan-valley.body:
On our second day in mid-Wales we went to Elan Valley and spent the journey in awe.

Elan Valley is a river valley known for its scenery and nicknamed the Welsh Lake District. It covers about 70 square miles (180 km²) of lakes and countryside, including the popular Elan Valley Trail, part of which joins National Cycle Route 81 (Lon Cambria).

In 2015 it was named one of the UK’s darkest sky parks — another reason to linger after sunset.
